minutes.headline: Commission agreed in consensus to ease solar panel review and approved revised guidelines with a new application form and fee.
minutes.summary: The commission approved its February minutes, heard the Historical Society's plan to salvage a cupola from a town-owned gas station building, and debated solar panel review in the district. It voted to commission a future guideline change on solar and approved revised district guidelines, which now go to the select board for a 35-day review. It also discussed 50 Main Street, recruiting a new member, and moving the May meeting to a Thursday.

public_comment.topic: Chair asked for public comment at the start; none was offered.
Chair noted no public closing comments.

votes.motion: Approve the minutes of the 13 February 2024 meeting as presented.
Change the guidelines to align with the consensus on solar installation; amended to commission adjusting the guidelines for solar as a future guideline change.
Approve the district commission guidelines, with the revised certificate to alter application and new determination of applicability form.

budget_items.what_was_said: The town has been unable to fill the land use director post because of its pay; the figure was described as a range around the low six figures.
The fee is based on one hour of processing plus the cost of posting a public hearing notice. No fee for a determination of applicability.
The town said it is fine with the salvage as long as it does not incur the cost of moving it.

decisions.decision: The chair will speak with Town Counsel and the planning board chair about solar regulation and the commission's authority; no motion was needed.
The chair will ask the town about moving to Thursday meetings, starting with the May meeting, to accommodate a prospective new member.
One commission member will meet the 50 Main Street owner privately, to be scheduled, before any further action.
The next meeting is set for 9 April.
The chair will draft the notification letter to property owners for discussion at the next meeting.
The commission took no position on the Historical Society salvaging the cupola, and the Society will tell the town manager.

what_happened.line: The commission approved revised district guidelines, with a new certificate to alter application and a new determination of applicability form; they now go to the select board for review.
The commission voted to commission a future guideline change on solar panels, after a consensus on easing review of installations in the district.
The chair will consult Town Counsel and the planning board chair on solar regulation and the commission's authority; no motion was needed.
The commission took no position on the Historical Society salvaging a cupola from the town-owned gas station building; the Society will tell the town manager.
One member will meet the 50 Main Street owner privately before any further action, and the next meeting is set for 9 April.

why_it_matters: Homeowners in the district who want solar panels may face a lighter review once the guideline change is written, and any property owner there will use the new application form and its fee, which is based on an hour of processing plus the cost of posting a hearing notice.
watch_next: The commission's next meeting on 9 April, where the chair is to bring a draft notification letter to property owners.
The select board's review of the approved guidelines, which the minutes describe as a 35-day review.
